cases.name: 1010-code_then_comment_on_one_line
cases.trap: a line holding both code and a comment is code

cases.name: 1020-comment_then_code_then_comment
cases.trap:
a line that opens with a block comment, holds code, and closes with another. The shape of every
generated table: '/* 00 */ 0x8d022e27, /* cps = 10.02 */'

cases.name: 1030-brace_and_trailing_comment
cases.trap: a line holding only a brace and a comment. The brace is not content, and the comment still is

cases.name: 1040-pairs_in_either_order
cases.trap:
four pairs of lines, each holding the same two things in opposite order: code and a comment, a
string and a comment, a brace and a comment, a semicolon and a wordless comment. The swap keeps
every span the same kind, so within each pair the two lines must classify identically, whatever
order a counter's own classifier reads them in. The string pair is the witness that words inside
a comment do not outweigh a string on the same line in either direction

cases.name: 1050-block_comment_holding_line_comment
cases.trap: a line comment inside a block comment is part of the block

cases.name: 1060-line_comment_holding_block_open
cases.trap: a block opener inside a line comment opens nothing

cases.name: 1070-block_comment_closed_then_line_comment
cases.trap:
a block comment opens and closes on one line and a line comment follows it. Nothing is outside
the two but the space between them, so the line is comment and holds no code

cases.name: 1080-block_close_touching_a_line_comment
cases.trap:
the '//' opening the line comment is formed on the '/' that closes the block comment, so the two
share a byte and no search for '//' yields both of the places it appears to be at. Case 1070 is
the same line with a space between them, and Pascal's '{ block }//trailing' is the same line
again with a closer that shares no byte with it

cases.name: 1090-block_comment_closed_after_a_line_comment
cases.trap:
'//*/' closes a block comment, because '//' means nothing inside one. It is the C idiom for
switching a block off and on again by adding one character in front of its closer

cases.name: 1100-close_touching_reopen_plain
cases.trap: a block comment closes and the next one opens with nothing between the two symbols

cases.name: 1110-close_and_reopen_with_a_space
cases.trap:
the same close and reopen as case 1100 with whitespace between the symbols, which must change
nothing

cases.name: 1120-close_then_code_then_stray_and_reopen
cases.trap: a block closes, code follows, then a stray close and a real open share a byte

cases.name: 1130-closer_in_code_with_nothing_open
cases.trap: a raw string closer sitting in code with nothing open is an ordinary string holding a hash

cases.name: 1140-three_slashes_are_one_comment
cases.trap: three slashes hold one line comment and not two overlapping ones

cases.name: 1150-doc_comment_opening_after_code
cases.trap:
a doc comment that opens on a line which already holds code. The line is code, and the block of
documentation that begins on it does not begin at its first character

cases.name: 1160-two_comment_pairs_of_one_language
cases.trap: each pair ends only at its own closer, the other pair's token inside it is text

cases.name: 1170-pascal_writes_two_pairs
cases.trap: each pair ends only at its own closer, the other pair's token inside is text

cases.name: 1180-cmake_bracket_comment
cases.trap: a counted bracket comment is closed only by an end carrying the same count

cases.name: 1190-nested_block_comment_that_does_not
cases.trap: the first closer really does end the block in C, which does not nest

cases.name: 1200-nested_block_comment_that_nests
cases.trap: an inner block does not end the outer one in a language whose pairs nest

cases.name: 1210-close_touching_reopen_nesting
cases.trap: the same close and reopen with a pair that nests, where the reopener must not be counted twice

cases.name: 1220-nested_block_comment_in_odin
cases.trap:
Odin block comments nest, so the first closer ends only the inner one and the text under it is
still inside the outer block

cases.name: 2010-comment_symbol_inside_string
cases.trap: a comment symbol inside a string is text

cases.name: 2020-string_symbol_inside_comment
cases.trap: an unmatched quote inside a comment opens nothing

cases.name: 2030-string_symbol_of_another_kind_inside
cases.trap: only the symbol that opened a string can close it, so the other kind inside is text

cases.name: 2040-comment_pair_opening_inside_a_string
cases.trap: a block comment opener inside a string opens nothing

cases.name: 2050-string_opening_after_block_close
cases.trap: a string beginning at the byte straight after a block comment closes

cases.name: 2060-backtick_template_holding_a_comment
cases.trap: a line comment symbol inside a template literal is text

cases.name: 2070-verbatim_string_crossing_lines
cases.trap: a verbatim string opens with one symbol and closes with another, across lines

cases.name: 2080-odd_triple_quote_count
cases.trap:
a docstring opened on one line and closed on another keeps the lines between out of the comment
count, since a string is not a comment

cases.name: 2090-docstring_holding_a_comment_symbol
cases.trap:
the # inside the docstring is text and not a comment symbol, and the docstring around it is a
triple quoted string like any other, opening a line on its own

cases.name: 2100-triple_quoted_data_not_documentation
cases.trap:
a triple quoted string that is data the program prints and not documentation, with its opening
symbol at the start of a line. Case 2090 is the same shape where the block really is
documentation

cases.name: 2110-here_string_holding_an_apostrophe
cases.trap:
an apostrophe inside a PowerShell here string. The body of a here string is literal and it ends
only at a closer sitting at the start of a line, so the apostrophe in the word is a byte

cases.name: 2120-heredoc_holding_an_apostrophe
cases.trap:
an apostrophe inside a heredoc body. A heredoc names its own closer at runtime, which no
declaration of comment and string symbols can express

cases.name: 2130-raw_string_holding_quotes
cases.trap: a raw string keeps the quotes inside it to itself

cases.name: 2140-raw_string_holding_its_own_closing_bracket
cases.trap:
the opening line closes its quotes, so only the raw pair itself keeps the block opener under it
from starting a comment that never ends. A lone ) inside does not end the string

cases.name: 2150-delimited_raw_string_names_its_own_closer
cases.trap: a delimited raw string names its own terminator, so no declared symbol can close it

cases.name: 2160-long_bracket_string_holding_a_comment_symbol
cases.trap:
Lua writes a string with the same long brackets its comments use, so the -- inside one is text
and the line holding the closing bracket is still the string

cases.name: 2170-lua_level_bracket_holding_plain_close
cases.trap: a counted bracket is closed only by an end carrying the same count

cases.name: 2180-lua_short_closer_hiding_the_real_one
cases.trap: a bare ]] must not hide the ]=] that begins one byte inside it

cases.name: 3010-escaped_quote_before_comment
cases.trap:
an escaped quote does not close the string, so the // after it is a real comment and not text
inside it

cases.name: 3020-multiline_string_ending_in_backslash
cases.trap:
a raw string whose last byte is a backslash, written with the same symbol at both ends. A
backtick string in Odin escapes nothing, so the second backtick closes it whatever precedes it

cases.name: 3030-raw_string_ending_in_backslash
cases.trap: a raw string ends at its own closer even when the last byte is a backslash

cases.name: 3040-bare_raw_string_ending_in_backslash
cases.trap:
the same closing backslash as case 3030, in the raw form that carries no hashes. The two forms
end the same way, so a reader that handles one and not the other is reading the hashes and not
the rule

cases.name: 3050-verbatim_string_ending_in_a_backslash
cases.trap:
a verbatim string whose last byte is a backslash. In F# the body of @"..." is literal, so the
closing quote closes it whatever precedes it, and the line ends where it looks like it ends

cases.name: 3060-wysiwyg_string_ending_in_a_backslash
cases.trap:
a wysiwyg string whose last byte is a backslash. In D the body of r"..." is literal, so the
closing quote closes it whatever precedes it, and the line ends where it looks like it ends

cases.name: 3070-backslash_before_a_closing_quote_in_sql
cases.trap: standard SQL escapes a quote by doubling it and the backslash is an ordinary character

cases.name: 3080-backtick_escapes_inside_a_double_quoted_string
cases.trap:
the backtick is what escapes inside PowerShell's double quoted string, so the quote in the middle
of the line closes nothing

cases.name: 3090-backtick_before_a_single_quoted_string
cases.trap:
the other PowerShell string form escapes nothing inside itself, so the backtick can only speak
outside it, where it stops the apostrophe from opening anything

cases.name: 4010-char_literal_holding_a_quote
cases.trap: the quote inside a character literal opens no string

cases.name: 4020-two_char_literals_holding_escapes
cases.trap:
two character literals on one line, one holding an escaped backslash and one holding a quote.
Ordinary Rust, and this exact line appears in mezura's own sources

cases.name: 4030-character_written_with_a_backslash
cases.trap: a quote written as a character with a backslash opens no string

cases.name: 4040-escaped_apostrophe_outside_quotes
cases.trap:
a backslash before an apostrophe in unquoted shell text, which is how one writes an apostrophe
without quoting it. Shell escapes with the backslash outside a string and not inside

cases.name: 4050-lifetime_and_apostrophe_in_string
cases.trap: two lone ticks on one line, a lifetime and the apostrophe of a word inside a string

cases.name: 4060-primed_identifier_haskell
cases.trap: a primed name beside a real character literal

cases.name: 4070-primed_identifier_ocaml
cases.trap: a primed name beside a real character literal, in a language whose comments are a nesting pair

cases.name: 4080-primed_identifier_and_apostrophe
cases.trap: a primed name beside an apostrophe inside a string, where neither tick may pair

cases.name: 4090-transpose_operator_and_char
cases.trap: the transpose operator is a lone tick and must not pair with the literal below it

cases.name: 5010-line_splice_inside_a_string
cases.trap:
a backslash at the end of the line continues the string in C, so the // inside it is not a
comment

cases.name: 5020-blank_line_inside_a_spliced_string
cases.trap:
the splice carries a string only off a line ending in a backslash, and the blank line does not,
so the string is over before the comment line

cases.name: 5030-line_splice_inside_a_comment
cases.trap: a backslash at the end of a line comment continues it onto the next line in C

cases.name: 5040-line_splice_in_a_comment_with_no_words
cases.trap:
the splice of case 5030 on a comment line holding no letter or digit at all, which is how a
decorative rule is written. What a line says has no bearing on whether it continues

cases.name: 5050-line_splice_after_a_closed_block_comment
cases.trap:
a block comment closes and a line comment opens on the same line, with a space between the two.
That space is not code, so the splice ending the line still carries the comment on

cases.name: 5060-code_then_a_spliced_line_comment
cases.trap: a line holding real code ends in a spliced line comment, so the next line belongs to that comment in C

cases.name: 6010-html_has_no_strings
cases.trap: HTML declares no string symbols, so an apostrophe in the text costs nothing

cases.name: 6020-comment_opener_inside_an_attribute
cases.trap:
a comment opener written inside a quoted attribute value, where HTML reads it as text. Nothing
closes it further down, so a counter that opened a comment there never ends one

cases.name: 6030-opening_tag_split_over_two_lines
cases.trap:
the opening tag is split over two lines, which is legal, and is not the opener any language file
declares

cases.name: 6040-script_tag_in_upper_case
cases.trap:
HTML reads its tag names without regard to case, so an upper case SCRIPT opens a script element
exactly as a lower case one does

cases.name: 6050-script_closer_written_with_a_space
cases.trap:
a closing tag written with a space before its bracket, which is legal and rare. It is not the
closer any language file declares, and all four totals are the same whether the block is found or
not, which is what hides it

cases.name: 6060-script_closer_inside_a_string
cases.trap:
a script element ends at the first closing tag whatever the JavaScript around it is doing, which
is why one writes the closer with a backslash inside a string. So the block here is empty and
everything under the closer is markup, including what looks like a comment

cases.name: 6070-script_opener_that_never_closes
cases.trap:
the text of a script tag written inside a paragraph, with no closing tag anywhere after it.
Nothing marks an opener as a tag rather than the same word written out, so a block that never
closes is text and the rest of the file belongs to the page

cases.name: 6080-block_named_by_a_mime_type
cases.trap:
a script tag can name its language with a mime type instead of a lang attribute, and a mime type
spells the language out: 'text/typescript', not 'text/ts'. The counts are the same whichever
language answers, so what this case is about is the label

cases.name: 6090-vue_blocks_count_as_their_own_languages
cases.trap:
one file, three languages: the script and style blocks are counted with their own symbols, so
the js comment and the css comment are comments although the Vue file holding them has neither
symbol

cases.name: 6100-block_language_named_by_the_tag
cases.trap:
the opener names the block's language, so this file is Vue, TypeScript and SCSS and not Vue,
JavaScript and CSS. The three totals are the same either way, which is why a case about labelling
has to declare its regions and not only its counts

cases.name: 6110-php_block_holding_html_around_it
cases.trap:
the file switches language at a tag rather than at a file boundary, and switches back at another
tag, so the markup between the two belongs to a language the extension does not name

cases.name: 6120-script_inside_html_inside_php
cases.trap:
three languages deep, the everyday shape of a page: the php file holds html between its blocks,
and the html holds a script. Every line belongs to the innermost language, and a tag's own line
to the language that encloses the tag, so the script tags are html and the html sits between the
php blocks

cases.name: 7010-regex_literal_holding_a_quote
cases.trap:
a quote inside a regex literal, which costs its own line at most where the language declares its
quotes as ending with the line

cases.name: 7020-regex_holding_a_comment_opener
cases.trap:
a comment opener inside a regex literal. Telling a regex from a division needs the token before
the slash, which is a lexer's job, and every counter measured here answers the same way

cases.name: 8010-punctuation_only_line
cases.trap:
a line holding only a brace. A definition, not a mistake: neither code nor comment to a counter
that asks what a line says, code to one that asks whether the file would compile without it

cases.name: 8020-blank_line_inside_block_comment
cases.trap:
a blank line inside a block comment. A definition, not a mistake: blank to a counter that asks
what a line says, comment to one that asks which block it sits in

cases.name: 8030-blank_line_inside_a_multiline_string
cases.trap:
a blank line inside a multi line string. A definition and not a mistake: blank to a counter that
asks what a line says, code to one that asks which region the line sits in

cases.name: 8040-doc_comment_with_no_text
cases.trap:
a doc comment line holding nothing but its marker, which is how a blank line is put between two
paragraphs of documentation. A bare marker says nothing, so it is extra to a counter that asks
what a line says

cases.name: 8050-doc_comment_with_no_text_ending_a_block
cases.trap:
the same empty doc comment line as case 8040, this time with no further documentation under it.
What makes it its own case is that the answer stops being about comments and becomes about
lines
